chunks: And what he narrated - Musa ibn al-Qasim said: Some of our companions informed me

that he asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) during the ten days of Shawwal, saying: 'I intend to perform an Umrah exclusively this month.' He said to him, 'You are held hostage by Hajj.' The man said to him, 'Indeed, Medina is my home and Mecca is my home, and I have family between them and wealth between them.' He said to him, 'You are held hostage by Hajj.' The man said to him, 'Indeed, I have orchards around Mecca and I need to go out to them.' He said, 'You go out in a state of permissibility (halal) and return in a state of permissibility (halal) for Hajj.'

For these two reports are interpreted as referring to one who had entered Mecca performing Umrah with the intention of enjoying it until Hajj, then wished to make it exclusive. And if the matter is as we mentioned, it is not permissible for him to do so because he is bound by Hajj. And in the report it is not stated that he said: 'I intended to make Umrah exclusive before entering it,' so he said to him, 'You are held hostage by Hajj.' And if that is not in the apparent meaning of the report and it is compatible with what we mentioned, then it is not contradictory to what we presented. And that which indicates this meaning is what he narrated:

key_terms.تَمَتُّعٌ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj)
key_terms.حَلاَلاً: In a state of permissibility (exiting Ihram status temporarily)
key_terms.ضِيَاعٌ: Orchards/Estates (plural of diya', referring to agricultural land or property)
key_terms.عُمْرَةٌ مُفْرَدَةٌ: Exclusive Umrah (Umrah performed independently, not as part of Tamattu')
key_terms.مُرْتَهَنٌ بِالْحَجِّ: Held hostage by Hajj (bound by the Hajj obligation, unable to fully exit Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who performs Umrah exclusively while still obligated to perform Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential nuance of *Hajj al-Tamattu'*, where the pilgrim is considered 'bound' (*murtahan*) to the Hajj obligation after performing Umrah. The Imam’s response indicates that one cannot isolate the Umrah ritual to the exclusion of the subsequent Hajr status, ensuring the continuity of the pilgrimage rite. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the inseparability of the two rites in the Tamattu' mode, distinguishing it from *Qiran* or *Ifrad*.
